en.title: Minimum Edge Reversals with Any Root
en.description:
You are given a tree where every edge currently has a direction. Choose any node as the root; all edges must end up pointing away from the root. Reversing one edge costs 1. Find the minimum total cost.

This site has made the standard input and output explicit; any range not given by the source is marked as this site's protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n, followed by n−1 lines of directed edges u v, 0-based. The source gives no upper bound; on this site 1≤n≤200000, and ignoring directions the graph must be a tree.
en.explanation: Example 1: whether 0 or 2 is the root, only 1 edge needs reversing, so the minimum is 1. Example 2: with 0 as the root all edges already point outward, so output 0. Example 3: there are no edges, so nothing needs reversing.
hints: First count the reversed edges with 0 as the root, then reroot: moving the root to a child along an originally forward parent-to-child edge costs one more reversal, and along an originally reversed edge costs one fewer.
